reason: The paper introduces a benchmark-agnostic methodology for evaluating research agents’ epistemic processes from execution records, measuring how their claims, experiments, and revisions relate to executed evidence.
The paper introduces intent-targeted tool signals to complement chain-of-thought monitoring, track emerging harmful intent during agent reasoning, and identify opportunities for intervention.

TRACE introduces an evidence-annotated safety benchmark for evaluating guardrail models across prompts, reasoning traces, and final responses, with particular emphasis on detecting unsafe content in reasoning traces.
The paper develops and applies a simulated safety evaluation of whether frontier models perform unauthorized supply-chain attacks against third-party targets.
The paper introduces and evaluates a trace-based failure-attribution method for locating the earliest security-relevant error in vulnerability-repair agents.
The paper studies how readily models learn to conceal reasoning in innocuous text, directly assessing a threat to chain-of-thought monitoring under different training pressures.
The paper studies and detects reward hacking using generalizable internal representation vectors, enabling inexpensive online monitoring of undesirable model behavior.
The paper evaluates whether chain-of-thought reflects the model’s actual internal computation by measuring shared concepts and causally ablating them to test their contribution to predictions.
The paper evaluates LLM oversight of other models, showing how procedural traces shift auditors’ decision criteria and false-alarm rates rather than simply improving error detection.

The paper proposes an auditable delegation protocol and reconstruction test for holding agents accountable, directly addressing how human oversight can distinguish substantive supervision from rubber-stamping.

The paper formalizes and evaluates the robustness of chain-of-thought faithfulness detectors, proposing an invariant detector and stress tests for auditing whether reasoning traces reflect actual model computations.
The paper evaluates whether language models knowingly conceal their own mistakes, directly studying deceptive omission in chat and agentic settings.
The paper develops and evaluates white-box probes for detecting deception, hidden goals, and sabotage in language models, with the aim of improving agent monitoring.
The paper theoretically and empirically analyzes when chain-of-thought content is computationally necessary for transformer reasoning, establishing task-dependent accuracy ceilings without it.
The paper introduces plan-injection attacks that conceal adversarial actions from chain-of-thought monitors and evaluates monitor evasion across tasks and models.
The paper detects unfaithful chains of thought by tracking premature answer commitment, identifying cases where models reach answers through shortcuts and then post-rationalize them.
The paper theoretically and empirically analyzes why RLVR induces language drift in reasoning traces, including the resulting trade-off between CoT monitorability and reward.
The paper develops counterfactual tests of whether vision-language models’ reasoning traces faithfully reflect the visual evidence that actually influences their predictions.
The paper argues for sandboxing and taint-tracking security guarantees independent of linguistic self-reports, while examining fundamental limitations of chain-of-thought monitoring.
The paper audits whether emitted chain-of-thought text causally mediates model decisions, using layerwise activation patching to identify reasoning windows and latent bypass pathways.
NeuronEye steers frozen vision-language models by selectively activating sparse visual concepts and suppressing competing representation directions to improve query-specific visual reasoning.
The paper introduces an inherently interpretable neural additive architecture for learning on hypergraphs, with node- and hyperedge-level prediction as its main tasks.
The paper systematically characterizes the geometry and hierarchical structure of LLM hidden-state representations using Gromov hyperbolicity across models, layers, and domains.
The main contribution is matching convergence bounds and a worst-case lower bound for row-normalized Muon optimization, with LLM pretraining serving as an empirical contrast.
The paper develops temporally coherent adversarial observation attacks against recurrent world-model reinforcement-learning agents using a low-dimensional subspace derived from the victim’s critic.
ORPG introduces a multi-objective policy-gradient method for language-model post-training, reconciling reward gradients across both helpfulness–safety alignment and mathematical reasoning objectives.
The paper studies the dimensionality of learned matrix-memory representations, using rank interventions to show that effective rank matches the task’s minimal faithful representation dimension.
The paper studies how retrieving demonstrations affects test-time adaptation and task performance of vision-language-action robot policies.
The paper audits a sycophancy benchmark, identifying prompt-template confounds that undermine its conclusions and proposing methodological checks for alignment evaluations.
The paper proposes and evaluates a reference-based methodology for relating coherence and diversity in open-ended text generation to human quality judgments.

The paper identifies and causally characterizes the attention, residual-stream, and MLP mechanisms that implement number comparison, showing how they use linear representations despite curved representational geometry.
The paper uses activation-importance signatures and clustering to investigate how LLMs internally organize mathematical reasoning, finding structure by reasoning approach rather than topic.
The paper introduces a mean-field analysis of attention to predict how representation geometry evolves across layers and quantify context-specific computation.
The paper uses residual-stream and attention-head patching to causally test whether encoded visual answers influence predictions and to distinguish mechanisms of vision-language model failure.
The paper develops a head-wise hybrid attention architecture grounded in functional analyses of Transformer heads, with improved zero-shot long-context extrapolation as a central outcome.
The paper trains an automated SAE-feature explainer using activation-guided feedback to iteratively verify and improve its explanations.
The paper introduces a diagnostic of layer-wise residual representation similarity and uses it to characterize correlated residual updates across language models.
The paper analyzes activation steering and shows that behavioral interference is governed by model defaults rather than the geometry or overlap of steering directions.
The paper systematically studies evaluation awareness, a threat to reliable capability and safety testing, through internal probes, verbalization measurements, and activation steering.
The paper identifies residual-stream representations of semantic exploration and exploitation, and uses activation steering to test and control category switching.
The paper discovers and causally validates animacy circuits in language models using controlled minimal pairs, circuit discovery, and ablation experiments.
The paper uses causal mechanistic analysis to identify and test layer-organized computations, information flow, and specialized attention heads underlying propositional reasoning in LLMs.
The paper introduces an optimal-transport method for discovering and testing causal correspondences between high-level models and neural components through interchange interventions.
The paper studies emergent misalignment caused by narrow fine-tuning and develops a geometry-based training intervention to suppress the resulting safety failures.

The paper uses sparse-feature ablations, causal patching, and routing interventions to show that harmful-meme classification failures often arise from represented evidence failing to reach the model’s output.
The paper compares layerwise attention-head activity patterns to understand internal information routing, without identifying specific representations or causally verified circuits.
The paper introduces a contrastive sparse autoencoder and evaluates whether its learned features capture functionally interchangeable reasoning representations across languages.
The paper evaluates the faithfulness objectives used in circuit discovery, showing that intervention-based metrics can misrank circuits and diagnosing the resulting mechanism-recovery gap.
The paper studies safety degradation during non-adversarial fine-tuning and tests activation-direction-based training objectives that suppress or amplify this degradation.
The paper introduces and validates a measurement criterion for separating intervention-site confounds from genuine activation interactions, improving the reliability of interpretability analyses.
The paper studies how scaling synthetic distillation datasets changes the transfer of latent teacher traits to students, with implications for training-data curation and evaluation.

The paper studies latent knowledge in residual-stream representations and its relationship to verbalized answers, using probes and causal ablations to distinguish linear decodability from causal control.
The paper introduces a benchmark and attack method for image-borne prompt injection in multimodal agent skills, measuring unauthorized actions alongside legitimate-task completion.

SafeLens develops a vision-language video moderation framework whose fast-and-slow inference architecture selectively allocates reasoning computation to improve accuracy while reducing inference cost.
The paper introduces a query-efficient black-box decoding attack that bypasses LLM safety alignment using sampled text and selective control of generation.
The paper develops and evaluates reinforcement-learning methods for alignment auditors that investigate models and uncover hidden or concerning behaviors while controlling false positives.
The paper introduces multimodal backdoor attacks through data and model poisoning of unified autoregressive models, demonstrating trigger-induced manipulation of both text and image outputs.
The paper introduces and validates a safety-monitor evaluation methodology focused on harmful requests the target model actually answers, exposing failures hidden by standard metrics.
InfiFPO introduces a DPO-based preference optimization method that fuses probability information from multiple source models to improve a pivot model’s alignment with human preferences.
The paper develops an agent-harness framework with enforced budgets, provable termination, and independently verified completion, supported by an instrument for testing its verification gates.
The paper introduces and evaluates a multimodal jailbreaking method and dataset for inducing harmful outputs from language models across text, vision, and audio.
The paper introduces an unlearning-based defense against jailbreak attacks that removes harmful knowledge while preserving general capabilities and safety alignment.
The paper studies evaluation awareness across model scales and mitigates it through prompt sanitization and activation counter-steering.

The main contribution is an unsupervised method for decoding intermediate computations from hidden-state representations during filler-token reasoning, supported by causal KV-cache interventions and implications for monitorability.
The paper evaluates safety guard calibration under adversarial attacks, showing that high-confidence classification failures persist despite uncertainty signals in corresponding base models.

The paper demonstrates that distillation on semantically unrelated data can covertly transfer backdoors and harmful behavioral traits, with additional experiments showing transfer of reward-hacking propensities.
The paper develops and evaluates structural best-of-N jailbreak attacks, analyzing how encoding, repeated sampling, and defense architecture affect safety robustness.
The paper introduces a controlled benchmark for evaluating tool-using agents’ post-failure reporting, measuring unsupported success claims, fabricated details, and useful recovery.
The paper develops and evaluates reward-shaping principles and a preference-based reward signal specifically to mitigate reward hacking and stabilize RLHF.
The paper develops a deployment-time safety defense that detects unsafe or novel inputs through anomaly detection using locally sparse SAE activations.
The paper experimentally analyzes why online RLHF outperforms offline preference optimization, focusing on the role of on-policy sampling in training helpful language models.
LEAF introduces span-level reinforcement-learning post-training for speech-aware language models, improving speech question answering and translation without additional decoding.

The paper introduces a teacher-intervention distillation method specifically for training multi-turn language-model agents, correcting supervision and sampling mismatches in mixed-policy interaction trajectories.
The paper introduces an on-policy distillation method specifically for training multi-turn language agents, using graph-indexed execution evidence to improve teacher supervision.
The paper improves reasoning distillation through Trajectory Dropout, a training intervention that strengthens teacher supervision on student-generated reasoning trajectories.
Trinity introduces self-play reasoning training with an EMA self-verifier that supplies image-grounded supervision and rewards to improve vision-language models without labeled data.
The paper primarily develops reward-trained abstention to reduce confident errors and calibrate language models’ willingness to answer, using a modified RLVR objective.
The paper proposes weak-model-generated reasoning prefixes to improve exploration and mitigate entropy collapse during RLVR training of language models.
The paper introduces a reasoning-distillation method that generates teacher-guided, student-compatible traces for supervised post-training of small reasoning models.
The paper analyzes what on-policy reasoning distillation transfers, showing that it improves compositional reasoning skills rather than expanding factual knowledge.
The paper introduces an architecture-aware credit-assignment and critic method for PPO-based language-model reinforcement learning, improving reasoning accuracy and training stability.
TTPO introduces a label-free policy optimization objective combining self-distillation and grouped reinforcement learning to improve mathematical reasoning through test-time training.

The paper introduces an on-policy distillation method specifically for visual agents, using trajectory-level diagnoses of image operations and subsequent reasoning to improve tool use and task accuracy.

The paper introduces a reinforcement-learning method for language-model reasoning that improves exploration through sparse corrections to otherwise on-policy rollouts, evaluated on math and code benchmarks.
DiffGate introduces a reasoning post-training objective that combines GRPO's verifiable outcome rewards with difficulty-gated teacher guidance to improve mathematical and coding solution coverage.
The paper introduces adaptive example selection and batch reweighting to improve reinforcement fine-tuning of language models for reasoning.
The paper develops contrastive self-distillation for reasoning, separating correctness signals from behavioral shifts to improve reasoning performance while stabilizing response length.
VERPO improves reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning by combining GRPO outcome rewards with evidence-guided, reward-aligned token-level credit assignment.
MetaEvolve primarily develops iterative self-refinement skills through reinforcement learning with execution-verifiable rewards, complemented by inference-time evolutionary search.

The paper introduces a research-level mathematics dataset and teacher reasoning trajectories, demonstrating that supervised reasoning training improves language models’ advanced mathematical capabilities.
The paper introduces and evaluates a prompt-injection attack that poisons agents’ persistent memory to trigger malicious actions and privacy leakage across sessions.

The paper introduces an executable environment for evaluating and training multimodal LLM agents on long-horizon courier planning, with persistent resource constraints, trajectory rewards, and an adaptive curriculum.

The paper introduces a decentralized communication and commitment protocol for coordinating embodied language-model agents with private information, improving cooperative task success and inference efficiency.
The paper introduces a framework for selecting and dynamically adapting reusable browser-automation APIs to improve web agents’ accuracy, efficiency, and alignment with user needs.
The paper studies how identity labels cause factionalism and reduce cooperation among interacting LLM agents, and evaluates withholding labels as a mitigation.
EdgeGen generates database-grounded edge-case task datasets for evaluating and improving tool-calling agents through automated fine-tuning and harness optimization.
Chronos improves repository-level coding agents by retrieving connected pull-request history to guide patch generation, validation, and multi-agent patch selection.
The paper introduces a selection-aware protocol for evaluating interactive-agent workflows and confirming stress-test findings on held-out tasks with statistical validity guarantees.

The paper introduces a trace-grounded safety evaluation methodology and benchmark for memory-related risks in long-horizon LLM agents, with subset selection that preserves rare high-severity failures.

The paper introduces hindsight-based supervision and proxy rewards for training long-horizon LLM agents to manage memory, using retrievals, citations, and deletion interventions to assign credit to memory operations.
The paper introduces a benchmark evaluating vision-language agents on long-horizon, multi-image identification through sequential questions, constraint tracking, and protocol-compliant interactions.
The paper evaluates emergent safety risks across multiple generative-agent interaction settings, showing that collective failures can arise despite individual-agent safeguards.
SERA trains cooperating parent and child language-model agents to decompose, solve, and evaluate delegated subtasks using learned rubrics and decomposition-specific credit signals.
The paper develops and evaluates language-model research world models that predict experimental outcomes to improve AI research agents’ experiment selection under limited execution budgets.
The main contribution is an open-weight retriever trained to gather and rank evidence through multi-round, tool-driven search for downstream answer generation.
The paper introduces a realistic privacy-safety evaluation framework with trajectory-level metrics for LLM agents, complemented by runtime auditing of privacy violations.
The paper introduces a budget-efficient compositional search method for improving language-model agent harnesses, focusing on modular agent architectures and orchestration rather than model weights.
The paper introduces a hierarchical decentralized framework for coordinating large populations of LLM-based agents, with privacy-preserving knowledge sharing and adaptive resource allocation.
The paper develops a structured textual world model for predicting long-horizon consequences of action sequences, enabling agents to plan and compare counterfactual futures.
The paper develops a training-free action reranker for embodied vision-language-action policies that preserves feasible routes to safe task completion.
The paper introduces a post-training quantization framework that improves LLM compression using refreshed gradient and Hessian estimates with stabilized gradient compensation.
The paper introduces a transferable fixed-bandwidth document-memory format that compresses external knowledge for efficient language-model reasoning while also supporting retrieval.
MoARa improves memory-efficient LLM pretraining through module-aware gradient projection ranks and structure-preserving decomposition, reducing training steps and wall-clock time.
DeltaS introduces a training-free KV-cache eviction method that uses linear-attention state drift to improve bounded-memory inference in streaming video-language models.
The paper develops and theoretically analyzes geometry-aware scheduling algorithms for memory-constrained LLM serving, improving inference latency and throughput through integration with vLLM.

The paper introduces a training-free spectral composition of thinking and non-thinking checkpoints that reduces inference token costs while preserving reasoning accuracy, supported by analyses of where reasoning capacity resides in model weights.
The paper introduces a training-free KV-cache eviction method that uses sampled future continuations to improve fixed-budget cache compression for language-model inference.

The paper introduces a training-free parallel decoding method for masked diffusion language models that improves throughput while preserving accuracy through stability-based token selection and entropy-budgeted commitment.
The paper introduces batch-aware expert selection for MoE decoding that reduces expert-weight transfers while preserving accuracy, directly improving language-model inference efficiency.
The paper evaluates the correctness, composability, updateability, and rebuilding costs of precomputed language-model memory based on saved and compressed key-value caches.
MoRA introduces structured expert pruning and post-pruning expert approximation to reduce MoE language models' deployment memory requirements while preserving performance.
LatentHarness introduces an adaptive latent-action architecture that unifies iterative reasoning, fast-weight memory recall, and token emission, with a clear contribution to long-context memory.
TRACE improves the efficiency of RL post-training through rollout-guided FP4 quantization-aware training that aligns training and rollout execution while reducing memory and communication overhead.
The paper introduces a two-tower transformer architecture and KV-invariant model expansion paradigm that improve scaling efficiency across training, prompt processing, and decoding.
The paper introduces activation denoising for parallel post-training LLM quantization, improving compression accuracy while avoiding the cost of sequential calibration.
The paper proposes a memory-efficient distributed MoE execution and recomputation system that improves training throughput and supports longer sequences under fixed GPU memory budgets.

The main contribution is a trajectory-aware training objective and recipe for masked diffusion language models that jointly optimizes consecutive denoising steps to reduce the train–inference mismatch.
ECHO accelerates LLM inference through speculative decoding that combines early-layer draft exploration with full-model verification and state reuse.
The paper develops a hardware–algorithm co-design for scalable analog Transformer training, combining mixed precision, optimizer changes, weight mapping, and converter calibration.
The paper introduces tokenizer vocabulary training and text segmentation methods that improve token efficiency while preserving downstream language-model performance.

The paper develops convergence theory and explicit rates for Riemannian ascent–descent in nonconvex–nonconcave minimax optimization, with distributionally robust statistical learning as its application.
MetaRTL introduces an efficient relational learning framework that uses non-parametric graph message passing and attention over meta-path features to model relationships across database tables.
The paper develops and compares physics-shaped hierarchical graph neural networks for power-flow prediction, with graph communication architecture as its main contribution.
The paper develops a performance-estimation and recalibration framework for molecular binding prediction to improve therapeutic discovery and experimental validation.
The paper proposes task- and structure-aware prompt initialization for pre-trained graph models, improving few-shot node and graph classification.
The paper introduces predictive representation learning and structured latent dynamics modeling for solving and extrapolating parametric PDEs.
The paper develops dynamics-aware flow matching for single-cell trajectory inference, using discrete transition graphs to recover continuous cellular dynamics.
The paper applies supervised learning and ensemble methods to stroke-risk prediction, with its main contribution focused on medical diagnosis.
The paper develops a structured eye-gaze representation learning model for clinical autism screening, making its main contribution an AI application to health.
The paper proposes an adaptive federated graph clustering method that coordinates global community anchors across clients while keeping their graph data private.
The paper develops and validates a machine-learning clinical decision support tool for personalized heart-valve selection to reduce postoperative complications in TAVR patients.
The paper develops stable Q-learning algorithms with infinite-dimensional linear function approximation and proves convergence bounds under Markovian sampling.
The paper proposes and evaluates structure-aware spreadsheet chunking to improve contextual interpretation and answer generation in LLM-driven retrieval-augmented generation systems.
The main contribution is a tabular diffusion model that incorporates weak semantic priors to improve synthetic tabular data fidelity and rule consistency.
The paper uses machine learning on recent HARQ feedback histories to predict retransmissions and improve 5G link adaptation, making its central contribution a time-series prediction application.
The paper develops and evaluates a digital twin framework using learned CT registration to forecast patient anatomy and enable clinically effective adaptive proton therapy.
The paper develops and evaluates a scribble-conditioned U-Net for interactive PET/CT lesion segmentation, making medical image segmentation its main contribution.

CAESAR contributes a general unsupervised clustering method that reorganizes pretrained embeddings and infers the number of clusters across text and image datasets, rather than studying language models themselves.
The paper develops an instruction-tuned LLM approach to argument mining that jointly extracts argumentative spans and classifies their components as a generative language task.
The paper improves diffusion-based image super-resolution by learning the noise sampling distributions used at intermediate denoising steps.
The paper develops reductions, bounds, greedy algorithms, and optimality certificates for a combinatorial constraint-solving problem on hypergraphs.
The paper develops a safety-constrained imitation-learning method for neural control policies and evaluates it on autonomous racing.
The paper develops and demonstrates prior-matched evaluation for an operational satellite-image classifier detecting rare internal-wave events.
The paper develops a diffusion Schrödinger bridge generative model for unpaired speech enhancement and waveform restoration.

The paper introduces a framework that combines protein generative priors with cryo-EM particle images to infer atomic biomolecular structures directly, making its main contribution AI for structural biology.
The main contribution is an asynchronous, pipeline-parallel framework for low-latency multilingual lip-synchronized video generation, rather than a language-model architecture or training method.
The paper introduces a self-supervised method for estimating dense distance and ego-motion from monocular fisheye video, making its main contribution to computer vision.
The paper extends symbolic music processing to capture expression annotations and supports generative music tasks such as joint expression-note generation and expression-conditioned composition.
The paper develops CNN- and GAN-based super-resolution methods and a cross-sensor dataset for downscaling satellite cloud masks, making its main contribution a remote-sensing computer vision task.
The paper establishes tight oracle-complexity lower bounds for stochastic nonconvex-strongly-concave minimax optimization, making its main contribution optimization theory.
The survey covers general machine-learning methods for incomplete, imbalanced, weakly supervised, and shifted data across multiple settings, without focusing on a single specialized subfield.
The paper proposes and analyzes an outlier-robust stochastic optimization method, proving convergence guarantees under convexity assumptions.
The paper benchmarks memory usage and resource-constrained performance of online classifiers for streaming tabular data, emphasizing bounded operation under concept drift.

The paper develops a fine-tuned LLM framework for manufacturing time-series generation, making its main contribution a domain application of language models with a substantive focus on time-series data.
The paper theoretically analyzes feature-augmentation boosting and establishes a hierarchy of calibration guarantees based on the expressivity of the augmented hypothesis class.
The paper studies lossy text compression as a language-model application, comparing strategic deletion methods and LLM decoders that reconstruct text from retained fragments.
The paper develops a learning method to recover interaction laws in particle systems from steady-state observations, enabling scientific system identification and reproduction of collective dynamics.
The paper applies distributed reinforcement learning to correct numerical weather forecasts within an operational atmospheric model, making its main contribution an AI application to weather science.
The paper establishes tight neuron-count bounds and near-optimal encoding complexity for neural approximation of Hölder-continuous functions.
The paper develops and analyzes an optimal-stopping peer-selection method for decentralized federated learning, with guarantees and experiments on evidence and communication efficiency.
The paper proposes a hierarchical aggregation framework for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning that improves coordination robustness under noisy observations.
DET introduces a generalized Bayesian framework for jointly inferring geometric deformation and functional alignment on irregular domains, demonstrated on spatial transcriptomics data.
The paper develops a diffusion-based synthetic tabular data generator with a causal-discrepancy training penalty to preserve treatment-effect inference alongside statistical fidelity.

The paper diagnoses and improves counterfactual input-response prediction in time-series foundation models through synthetic forced-system fine-tuning and comparisons with classical system identification.
The paper introduces a benchmark evaluating multimodal models’ ability to distinguish textual evasion from vocal confidence in earnings-call responses.
The paper provides a smoothed complexity analysis of A* search with inconsistent heuristics, a fundamental classical AI search algorithm.
The paper introduces a Bayesian contextual-bandit algorithm that handles structured non-stationarity by correcting and reweighting historical rewards.
The paper introduces LoRA fine-tuning and specialized losses for controllable lighting edits in a flow-matching diffusion image model.
The paper studies decidability and type-checking for formal tree transformations, a theoretical computer science topic outside the tree’s AI and machine-learning classes.
The paper proposes a causal discovery method that uses semantic variable tags and identifiable data structures to orient edges beyond the Markov equivalence class.
The paper characterizes the identifiability and downstream costs of errors in sampling-certified world models, proving how reachability constrains what certification can establish.
The paper proposes adaptive offline reinforcement learning, reframing offline-trained policies as priors that retain the capacity to improve through subsequent online interaction.

The paper introduces interpretable graph-derived node features and evaluates their applicability to node classification, with a substantial application to drug-target prioritisation in protein interaction networks.
The paper studies geographic bias in German news coverage of landslides, rather than AI systems, machine learning methods, or their societal effects.
The paper studies and improves cross-lingual transfer for scientific sentence classification across 13 non-English languages by exploiting shared rhetorical structure.
The paper develops a model-based policy-learning method that optimizes sparse feedback controllers through a differentiable constrained predictive-control objective.
The paper evaluates the validity of LLM-based diagnosis of student failure modes in mathematics tutoring dialogue, a domain-specific educational application of language models.
The paper introduces a task-adaptive decoder for frozen multimodal language-model representations, improving downstream prediction under limited supervision.
The paper characterizes the geometry of full conformal prediction regions and develops certified radial reconstruction methods for these uncertainty sets.
The paper evaluates time-series forecasting transfer between CNC machines with partially overlapping sensor channels, focusing on latent predictive pretraining, input normalization, and calibration.
The paper develops a formal voting framework based on defeasible argumentation and proves representation and computational-complexity results, fitting symbolic reasoning and knowledge representation.

The main contribution is a general contraction-based framework establishing finite-time convergence guarantees for stochastic bootstrapping operators, with temporal-difference learning as an application.
The paper develops and evaluates survival models for time-to-repurchase prediction on large-scale tabular e-commerce data, focusing on temporal ranking and probability calibration.
The paper introduces coupled robot-dynamics and wireless-channel world models for communication-efficient, resilient remote robotic control and navigation.
The paper introduces a general-purpose black-box optimization method that uses a fixed generative prior to improve search under strict objective-evaluation budgets.
The paper develops a real-world ultra-low-dose lung CT dataset and a purification-based denoising framework to improve medical image reconstruction.

The paper evaluates neural surrogates for a coupled neutrino radiation-hydrodynamics solver, identifying end-to-end runtime, distribution-shift, and fidelity barriers to accelerating scientific simulation.
The paper introduces and analyzes a communication-efficient federated multi-objective optimization method that weights competing tasks using objective slacks.

The paper develops and evaluates an attribution framework for EEG foundation models, with a focus on clinical reliability and neurophysiological plausibility rather than language-model interpretability.
The paper develops and validates a reinforcement-learning controller for quadrupedal robots transporting unsecured payloads across uneven terrain.
